event.name: 24 May 2014 North Aegean Sea (Samothraki) earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Dextral motion on the western North Anatolian Fault, North Aegean Sea, across multiple step-over structures.

reference.title: Structural setting along the Western North Anatolian Fault and its influence on the 2014 North Aegean Earthquake (Mw 6.9)

inversion.method: Geodetic inverse modelling from 45 coseismic GPS measurements with steepest-descent/gradient and Laplacian smoothing (smoothing parameter 0.15). This record digitizes Figure 7C, not the published numerical slip table.
inversion.green_function_model: Not specified in the publication (GPS displacement slip inversion).
inversion.notes: IMPORTANT: This JSON is a visualization-oriented figure reconstruction. The original paper has 378 slip patches on a nominal 200-km-long, 25-km-deep multisegment target fault, but their subfault layout cannot be recovered from Figure 7C. The 42 × 9 image sampling here coincidentally totals 378 cells; it MUST NOT be interpreted as the authors original 378-element mesh. Longitude-to-km uses 85.3 km/degree at 40 degrees N; down_dip_km is the DISPLAYED VERTICAL DEPTH axis, NOT distance down the physical fault plane. No patch geographic locations or trustworthy planar strike/dip can be inferred from this longitude-depth projection. The fault_segments object is a browser-compatible schematic raster carrier only. Figure 7C uses a continuous color scale from 0 to about 75+ cm, and overlays white PRE-SEISMIC contours, not coseismic contours. Values were estimated by matching RGB palette colors and masking white lines. Regional maximum ~90 cm and area-averaged mean ~25 cm are AUTHOR-REPORTED metrics and not matched exactly by figure colorbar sampling. Figure 7 plots one fault coordinate cross-section despite the event rupturing three fault segments with step-overs. DO NOT use this digitized model for seismic moment or dislocation calculations. The paper mentions original supplementary source Supplementary-coseismic-slip.txt, which was not available here; prefer that for exact patches.

provenance.compiled_by: Figure 7C colorbar reconstruction, Bulut et al. (2018), user-provided PDF; QA documentation included. This is NOT the original numerical inversion.
